questions.q: The basic unit of life is?
questions.exp: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms. Robert Hooke first discovered and named cells in 1665 while looking at cork under a microscope.
DNA stands for Deoxyribonucleic Acid. It is the molecule that carries genetic information in living organisms. Its double helix structure was discovered by Watson and Crick in 1953.
Insulin is produced by the beta cells in the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas. Insulin regulates blood sugar levels. Insufficient insulin production leads to diabetes mellitus.

questions.q: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.exp: The human heart has 4 chambers: two upper chambers called atria (left atrium and right atrium) and two lower chambers called ventricles (left ventricle and right ventricle).

questions.q: Which blood group is called the universal donor?
questions.exp: Blood group O negative (O-) is called the universal donor because it can be donated to any blood group. AB positive is the universal recipient as it can receive from all blood groups.

questions.q: Photosynthesis occurs in which part of the plant?
questions.exp: Photosynthesis primarily occurs in the leaves, in the chloroplasts. Chlorophyll (the green pigment) absorbs sunlight to convert CO₂ and water into glucose and oxygen.

questions.q: The longest bone in the human body is?
questions.exp: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest, heaviest, and strongest bone in the human body. It can support up to 30 times the body weight.

questions.q: Which vitamin is produced by the skin in sunlight?
questions.exp: Vitamin D is produced in the skin when exposed to ultraviolet B (UVB) rays from sunlight. It is essential for calcium absorption and bone health.

questions.q: The process by which plants lose water through leaves is called?
questions.exp: Transpiration is the process by which plants lose water vapor through their leaves (mainly through stomata). It helps in the upward movement of water and minerals from roots to leaves.

questions.q: The study of fungi is called?
questions.exp: Mycology is the branch of biology that deals with the study of fungi. Fungi include mushrooms, yeasts, and molds. They play an important role in decomposition and nutrient cycling.
